Alright, let me think this through as myself — as a woman who's been working these fields for thirty years and knows what the land does.

---

## My thinking

I'm 47 years old, the old man and me are the only ones in the fields now — the children work in the city and send money home sometimes, but in the fields it's just the two of us. 36 mu is too much for two people, honestly. So I plan carefully and I don't try anything fancy. I do what worked last year. That's how we've always done it.

**How I split the land.** The big field out west, the soil's sandier and good for cotton, so that's my cotton — about 16 mu. Cotton is the money crop, that's what pays for the fertilizer and the school things and everything else. The field closer to the village, flatter, easier water — that's maize, about 14 mu. And the small corner piece where the water doesn't reach well, I put 6 mu of mungbean. Mungbean doesn't ask for much, and we eat some and sell some at the market in summer.

**Cotton (16 mu).** We plant around mid-April, after Qingming, when the soil is warm enough you can stand on it without your feet getting cold. Buy the seed at the supply shop — the same kind my sister-in-law's family uses, about 50 yuan a mu. Before planting, we spread 1.5 bags of compound fertilizer per mu, the yellow 15-15-15 bag, same as always. Then when the cotton flowers in July I put down half a bag of urea per mu if the leaves look pale. The old man sprays for bollworm and aphids three or four times through the summer — we walk the rows and look. If we see bugs, we spray. Water it twice, maybe three if June is dry — but pumping is not cheap, the electricity adds up, so we don't run the well more than we have to. Picking cotton in September and October, we can't do alone — I hire four or five women from the village for maybe a week, pay them by the kilo.

**Maize (14 mu).** Since we don't have wheat before it, we plant spring maize — put it in the ground in early May. Use the yellow hybrid seed, the one with the red bag, neighbor Wang used it and got good maize last year. Hire the planter-machine to come through, it costs a bit but by hand two people can't plant 14 mu in time. One bag of compound with the planting, then half a bag of urea at knee-high when it shoots up. Water it once around tasseling if there's been no rain. Harvest end of August with the hired harvester. Maize is the easy one — much less work than cotton.

**Mungbean (6 mu).** Plant in June when the rains come. Scatter a little compound fertilizer — just a half-bag per mu, mungbean makes its own nitrogen so you don't need much, my mother-in-law taught me that long ago. Pull the big weeds by hand in July. Harvest in August, dry it on the threshing floor for a few days. Not a lot of money in mungbean but it's good to have.

**What I give up.** If I put more fertilizer on cotton, I'd maybe get more cotton, but then if prices drop I've spent money for nothing. If I irrigate more, the electric bill goes up. If I hire more help I have less cash at the end of the year. So I do the middle way — enough to get a decent harvest, not so much that one bad year ruins us. That's how my mother did it, that's how I do it.
